memo.verdict: Park. Neutral; conviction medium. The record parks Vestas Wind Systems (VWS-DK) on the return, not on the gates: at 200.20 DKK (26.78 EUR) the modal path pays about 9.6 percent a year over eighteen months and 9.2 percent a year over three years against the framework's 20 percent bar, and the re-rating that would close the gap is possible, not probable. None of the four park-rule gates fires (management B, business quality C, predictability B, trackability C). Re-engage on either of two triggers: a price below about 175 DKK with the thesis intact (the eighteen-month path then clears the bar at 15 times), or two consecutive quarters of Service margin expansion of 50 basis points or more with net contract assets declining. Exit the watch on a Service margin below 15.5 percent in any quarter, a second platform incident on the V236, or FY2027 guidance with an EBIT margin midpoint below 9 percent. Conviction is medium because the business judgement is firm and the valuation judgement rests on a multiple assumption the market could overrule in either direction within a quarter.
case: Vestas is a self-help margin recovery in a consolidated Western wind industry, and most of it has already happened. The change is internal, broad and in the reported numbers: a chief executive in post since August 2019 has run the 2021 value-over-volume strategy through the Operating Model Reset of 2025 and 2026 (900 white-collar roles cut in 2025, about 1,000 more in 2026; special items 62 EURm in 2025, 35 EURm Q1 2026, 27 EURm Q2 2026) and a Service recovery plan to end-2026. Warranty provisions fell from 6.4 percent of revenue (2022) to 3.2 percent (2025) and 3.0 percent (Q2 2026), with Q2 2026 consumption of 218 EURm exceeding new provisions of 141 EURm; SG&A is 7 percent of revenue; order ASP was 1.02 EURm per MW in Q2 2026 against Nordex's 0.91; renegotiated Service contracts were repriced 20 to 30 percent, new Service contracts up double digits, parts up to 15 percent, with 1.1 bn EUR of indexation in the Service backlog. The FY2026 EBIT margin guide was raised on 12 August 2026 to 7 to 9 percent from 6 to 8 percent, about 210 EURm of EBIT at the midpoint; buybacks stepped up four times in twelve months; the payout floor was raised to 40 percent. Five of the twelve internal screen forces are strong, the red flags are absent, and the one absent force is a chief-executive change.

The external forces help on structure and hurt on cost and in the United States. GE Vernova's halt to new offshore orders (November 2024) left a Vestas and Siemens Energy duopoly in European offshore; Western price wars have ceased; the top four Western OEMs are projected at about 94 percent of the ex-China onshore market by 2028; Germany awarded a record 14.4 GW onshore in 2025 and committed to 12 GW of extra volume over 2027 to 2029 (15 GW auctions planned in 2027 and 2028); Denmark cleared 1.8 GW in August 2026 on two-sided CfDs. Against: the US Department of the Interior paid over 1.4 bn USD to cancel about 4 GW of offshore leases; Section 232 moved to a 50 percent tariff in April 2026 with about 50 percent of potential US onshore orders on hold; steel up 32 percent and copper up 18 percent year-to-date; the European utility risk-free rate at 5.0 percent, up 86 basis points year-to-date, delaying developers' final investment decisions. Supply side D (bearings with SKF, Schaeffler and Timken; vessel shortages from 2026; Tianjin historically 75 percent of generator supply; 75 to 85 percent of rare earths from China), macro D, demand C (ex-China installations 48 GW in 2025 to 76 GW by 2030, 9 percent a year; US onshore pipeline 12 GW to 10 GW), competition B, own cycle B (revenue 14,486 EURm FY2022 to 18,822 EURm FY2025; Q2 2026 plus 26.1 percent).

The 'Financial Outputs' have followed in the chain's order to the sell-side layer. Margin A: minus 8 percent (2022), 4.3 percent (2024), 5.7 percent (2025), consensus 8.4 percent (2026), 9.5 percent (2027), 10.2 percent (2028), 10.6 percent (2029); the one margin not rising is Service (16.3 percent Q1 2026, 16.6 percent Q2 2026, against a 25 percent long-term target). Cash conversion B (FactSet free cash flow 1,410 EURm in FY2025, 181 percent of net income; consensus 90 to 105 percent for FY2026 to FY2028; caution: Service net contract assets 1,168 EURm at end-2025 because billing lags cost). Net debt B (net cash since 2024; buybacks 282 EURm in 2025, 222 EURm in H1 2026). Revenue growth C (plus 13.3 percent in 2026, then plus 7.5, plus 3.0, plus 5.7 percent consensus; our path plus 7, plus 4, plus 5 percent). Goldilocks growth B (FY2027 over FY2026 plus 21 percent; FY2026 to FY2029 about 14.4 percent a year; the six-month rate about plus 23 percent half on half, treated as cyclical). Sell-side upgrades C: the Q2 beat is written in (FY2027 consensus EPS plus 17.3 percent in six months), our path is 2 to 4 percent below consensus, guidance brackets consensus (8.4 percent against a 7 to 9 percent range), and the one-month revision is flat with one cut; the upgrade record is two-sided (cuts in 2021, 2022, August 2024, the February 2026 Service guide; beats on FY2024 revenue, the FY2025 margin, Q1 and Q2 2026; management an honest tracker with a conservative bias). Staircase B: dated steps in every window (11 November 2026 results; the 400 EURm buyback to 16 December 2026; a possible Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners stake sale, book value about 500 EURm; the UK AR8 budget; a Section 232 decision that could release 5 to 8 GW of US orders by end-FY2027; FY2027 guidance in February 2027; the end of the Service recovery plan; offshore break-even in 2027; 15 GW German auctions; a 10 percent margin and a 20 percent Service margin as far steps the market already assumes).
counter_case: The bull, at its strongest, is Redburn's: consensus is too low. FY2027 EBIT of 2,138 EURm and FY2028 EBIT of 2,442 EURm, 12 and 15 percent above consensus (22 May 2026), with an FY2028 margin of 10.7 percent, on mechanisms the record itself concedes are real: the Service book rotates onto post-reset pricing (about 45 percent of serviced capacity by 2030), with new contracts priced to the 25 percent target, renegotiations at plus 20 to 30 percent and 1.1 bn EUR of indexation in the backlog, against a consensus that carries only 19.2 percent for 2028, each 100 basis points of Service margin being about 3 percent of EPS; offshore reaches break-even in 2027 as five active projects are delivered, 52 V236 units are already installed and management calls offshore by far the largest lever; onshore pricing holds because the Western price wars have ceased; buybacks run at 5 percent a year on a net-cash balance sheet; and the 20 percent discount to capital-goods multiples (11.1 times 2027 EV/EBITA, Morgan Stanley; a 23 percent discount to Nordic peers, Redburn) closes. On that path FY2028 EPS is about 2.15 EUR, 24-month-forward earnings at eighteen months about 2.4 EUR, and a multiple of 18 to 18.5 times, the five-year median and about parity with capital goods, gives a value of about 44 EUR, 65 percent above today and 25 percent-plus a year. The evidence for it is the evidence the record relies on: Q2 2026's 117 percent EBIT beat, warranty consumption running ahead of provisions, a record Service backlog of 40.9 bn EUR, the GE Vernova exit, a guidance raise the sell-side still calls conservative (Jefferies: the midpoint implies only a 40 basis point H2 Power Solutions improvement), DNB Carnegie modelling 8.4, 9.4 and 10 percent for 2026 to 2028 with Service as the lever to beat consensus. The 'Compounder' setup's one passing condition, a named mis-modelled Service line (B), is this argument in the framework's own terms, and if it is right the correct box is 'Compounder' and the correct action is to buy before the Service margin inflects, not to park. The record concedes: the Service repricing mechanism is real, under-modelled and the one named line where consensus could be materially wrong; the offshore duopoly is a structural change the market may under-price; management has earned the benefit of the doubt on guidance since 2025; and a bounded-downside argument from the Service annuity is one a reader will raise. The record holds because the reported Service margin has not moved in three years and fell 60 basis points year on year to 16.6 percent in Q2 2026; because consensus already carries 19.2 percent for 2028, so the first two points of inflection are priced; because the Q3 2026 order shortfall (2,754 MW against 4,554 MW) and the US hold cap the volume side the bull's revenue needs; because the capital-goods multiple belongs to businesses with 15 to 20 percent margins and no first-of-kind 15 MW platform at the physical limit; because the two-year median of 13.86 times is the market's own judgement of this business through its recovery; and because Service EBIT of about 581 EURm for FY2026 is worth 6.2 to 8.8 bn EUR at 14.0 to 20 times post-tax earnings (23 to 33 percent of market capitalisation) or about 6.4 bn EUR at 11.1 times EV/EBITA (26 percent of enterprise value), so the annuity does not bound the downside at any defensible multiple and the case rests on Power Solutions' margin. The record puts the bull branch at about one in four; it is why the recommendation is a park rather than a rejection, and why the Service margin is the first leading indicator.

The bear, the second case against, is the risk research's false-friend profile: the headline beats mask structural Service decay, evidenced by 1.17 bn EUR of net contract assets unmatched among Western peers (Nordex carries net contract liabilities), a Service margin of 16.3 to 16.6 percent against a 25 percent target, Service revenue down 5.5 percent year on year against a record backlog (an outlier in the bottom 5 percent of aftermarket backlog-to-revenue conversion, the pattern that preceded the 312 EURm write-down of 2024), an 18-month hedging horizon against GE Vernova's 14 years, a share loss from 30 to 25 percent, and a V236 ramp that has already produced a three-to-four-month delay, a blade detachment and tower oscillation issues on a platform at the limit of blade speed, where multi-billion warranty provisions are the research's own phrase. On this reading the Q3 order shortfall is the first cockroach and the forming 'cyclical' and 'one-two' patterns are confirming; the bear targets of 130 to 132 DKK (Jefferies, Morgan Stanley, Redburn's downside) or 14.71 EUR (Barclays, Oddo) are reached on a 7 to 8 percent margin cap and EPS near 1.1 EUR at a 12 to 12.5 times trough multiple, about 100 DKK on the bear EPS, and a mark-to-market fall of a third to 9.83 times is possible with earnings unchanged. The record concedes the Q3 order and Service revenue data fit this shape and that the contract-asset build is the single accounting fact it would most want explained. It holds the bear at possible (about one in four) rather than probable because warranty consumption exceeding provisions is the opposite of deferred maintenance, the Q2 beat was in Power Solutions where the accounting is straightforward, the shortfall is one quarter against a backlog covering 2026 and most of 2027 with a specific and testable explanation (procurement timing, US holds, offshore awards paused to Q4), the contract assets are disclosed and the repricing is visible in signed contracts, and estimates have been cut by one house, not all. If Q3 shows a Service margin below 15.5 percent or a second platform incident, the record says its response fails and the case moves to D.
triggers: - Re-engage: a price below about 175 DKK (23.4 EUR) with the thesis intact, where the eighteen-month path clears 20 percent a year at 15 times; or two consecutive quarters of Service margin expansion of 50 basis points or more from Q4 2026 with net contract assets declining, which moves the re-rating branch to probable and the return to the bar's neighbourhood at today's price.
- Exit the watch: Service margin below 15.5 percent in any quarter; a second V236 platform incident; FY2027 guidance (February 2027) with an EBIT margin midpoint below 9 percent.

- The 11 November 2026 results test the company's explanation of the Q3 order shortfall (procurement timing, US holds, offshore awards paused to Q4), the H2 Power Solutions margin against the 9.5 percent the guide implies, and whether the sell-side cuts broadly after Deutsche Bank's 3.6 percent.

- Offshore break-even in 2027: watch Power Solutions margin, He Dreiht, Baltic Power and Nordseecluster milestones, vessel delays, warranty provisions (Alarm above 4 percent of revenue in a quarter; Invalidate a charge above 300 EURm for a named platform); what would change our mind is a second incident, a delay citing vessels, or a provision above 4 percent.

- Service margin: 50 basis points a quarter sequential from Q4 2026 moves offshore-plus-Service to probable and the case to progress; consensus has 19.2 percent for 2028, so a move to 19 percent is priced and 21 percent is not; Alarm below 15.5 percent; Invalidate below 15 percent for two quarters; contract assets Alarm above 1.3 bn EUR.

- Orders: two more quarters below 3 GW is bearish (Alarm below 3,000 MW for two consecutive quarters; Invalidate FY2027 revenue guidance below 22 bn EUR); a Section 232 outcome releasing the US pipeline (Jefferies' 5 to 8 GW by end-FY2027) is bullish and not in the modal path; consensus FY2027 revenue of plus 7.5 percent needs orders back above 4 GW a quarter by early 2027.
